PullRequest.Title: agentHost: use session-owned Copilot Connector accounts
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Use session-owned Copilot Connector accounts so ordinary GitHub.com token rotation does not require restarting the shared Copilot SDK client.

Related to #341199, #341007, and #340468. This addresses the Connector authentication trigger; it does not change per-client action dispatch ordering or make history reads independent of SDK session restoration.

- Pass static or refreshable credentials at the SDK session level for GitHub.com, including when Connectors are enabled.
- Select the session's opaque Connector account through `session.rpc.connectors.getAccount()` rather than enumerating global accounts and matching tokens.
- Retain Enterprise client authentication and safe deferred restarts for startup configuration changes, credential-mode changes, and failed credential updates.
- Check `sessionAccountSelection` before using the API. Log and skip Connector reconciliation for unsupported runtimes or unavailable accounts without blocking ordinary chat.
- Cover creating and restoring sessions after credential changes while another chat remains busy, plus Connector enablement and Enterprise restart safeguards.

Adopts github/copilot-agent-runtime#23010, already included in the pinned SDK. No dependency manifest changes.

## Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- Focused unit tests — **139 passed, 1 pending**:

  ```sh
  env -u COPILOT_HOME ./scripts/test.sh \
    --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts \
    --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts \
    --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotGitHubCredentials.test.ts \
    --grep 'Connector|connector|credential|authentication|restart on startup config change|CopilotGitHub' \
    --reporter dot
  ```

- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotSessionLauncher.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

The initial build/type-check encountered stale local SDK dependencies. `npm run install-fast` restored the existing declared dependencies, after which validation passed. A subsequent source edit only added an explanatory comment.

Live Connector integration and the full UI blocking scenario were not run.

## Manual verification

1. Launch the changed Code OSS build, sign in to GitHub.com, and enable Copilot Connectors before starting test chats.
2. Connect an available Connector, start a fresh Copilot Agent Host chat, and verify an actual successful Connector tool invocation.
3. Keep another chat active, for example waiting for an `ask_user` response. Supply a changed valid same-account token to the same Agent Host without signing out or toggling Connector enablement.
4. Open a nonresident saved chat and send a prompt in another new chat from the same window. Both should proceed without first ending the busy chat. Verify the busy chat can still receive input or cancellation.
5. Check the Agent Host log for successful Connector reconciliation and absence of a Connector token-only shared-client restart wait.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Ordinary GitHub.com Connector token rotation was treated as client-level authentication, scheduling a shared Copilot runtime restart. Restart safety deferred teardown until every active turn/subagent completed, while subsequent session acquisition waited on the pending restart waiter, coupling new chat creation/restoration to unrelated long-running chats and then incurring subprocess teardown/startup.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: After GitHub.com token rotation, opening or restoring another Agent Host chat could remain blocked for the lifetime of an unrelated busy chat, followed by shared runtime restart latency.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The changed branch leaves clientAuthenticationReason undefined for GitHub.com, supplies credentials in each SDK session, and updates live static-token sessions without restarting the shared CopilotClient. New create/restore work therefore no longer waits for an unrelated busy chat or pays subprocess teardown/startup solely for Connector token rotation; Enterprise and credential-mode changes retain the deferred restart path.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision, GitHub.com token changes with Connectors enabled set clientAuthenticationReason to 'Copilot Connector authentication updated', making restartRequired true and calling _requestClientRestart. That method parks the restart while any chat has in-flight work; _ensureClientForSession then loops and awaits _pendingClientRestartWaiter, so creating or restoring another session is blocked until the unrelated busy chat ends and the shared runtime is stopped. The added create/restore test at copilotAgent.test.ts:10310-10406 exercises this exact busy-chat path and asserts zero client stops plus immediate session launch after rotation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or restore a GitHub.com Copilot Connector chat, including immediately after token rotation while another chat is busy
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Acquire the shared CopilotClient, create/resume the SDK session, apply script-safety and sandbox options, then complete Connector capability/account lookup and reconciliation before publishing the session. The PR removes the pending shared-client restart from this path after ordinary GitHub.com token rotation, so unrelated busy chats are no longer on the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start or reuse the Copilot runtime process
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero starts on the warm-client path; one start on cold launch. Before the fix, a Connector token rotation could force one stop and later one restart after all busy chats completed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: GitHub.com Connector credentials were client-owned, so a changed token scheduled a shared-client restart and _ensureClientForSession could wait for the pending restart.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold startup remains critical. The diff removes token-only teardown/restart and its wait behind unrelated in-flight work from warm GitHub.com Connector launches.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One normal RPC per launch; resume can retain its pre-existing bounded fallback/retry behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same create/resume RPC occurred, but session credentials were omitted for GitHub.com Connectors because authentication lived on the client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the chat model/session can be used; placement and count are unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Connector getCapabilities, session-owned getAccount, and reconcile with catalog refresh
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three sequential session RPCs on a successful Connector launch; one capability RPC when unsupported and two through a missing account. Reconciliation remains once per session, not once per connector.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: After capabilities, launch performed gitHubAuth.getStatus and client.rpc.account.getAllUsers before the same reconcile call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These calls remain on finalization's critical path. The new getAccount replaces the old sequential gitHubAuth.getStatus plus client account enumeration, reducing successful-path lookup from two account-identification RPCs to one.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one refresh request per successful Connector session launch; failure falls back to one status RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same reconcile({ refreshCatalog: true }) operation was awaited once per Connector launch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reconciliation was already awaited before launch completion; the diff changes only account selection and does not increase refresh cardinality.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One create/resume sequence per requested resident chat. Connector work is one grouped reconciliation for the session/account, independent of connector count except for the returned catalog/status payload.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Operations within one launch are awaited sequentially. Independent session launches share the client and are not newly globally serialized by this diff; the PR explicitly leaves action dispatch ordering unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: An already-running client is reused. Session/account selection is resolved per newly created or resumed session; no new cache is added. Connector catalog refresh remains explicitly requested once per launched session. Unsupported runtimes and missing accounts terminate reconciliation without retries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed credential construction, restart gating, launcher RPC sequence, and tests directly establish the path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact runtime IPC and catalog-refresh duration depends on SDK/runtime state, but the before/after call counts and removal of the restart wait are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The change removes a global restart/wait mechanism and replaces two account-identification RPCs with one session-owned lookup while preserving one reconciliation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rotate GitHub.com credentials while multiple Connector-backed chats are resident
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The authentication RPC is serialized by the authentication sequencer. For same-mode static credentials it updates each resident static-token SDK session before resolving SKU and completing authentication; provider-backed sessions consume the refreshed provider token and are skipped. Unlike before, ordinary Connector rotation does not schedule or await shared-client teardown.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: session.rpc.gitHubAuth.setCredentials for each live static-token session
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sequential RPC per resident static-token session on an actual token change; zero for unchanged tokens and provider-backed sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: With Connectors enabled, token rotation skipped per-session updates, scheduled a global client restart, and could block new session acquisition until unrelated active turns/subagents ended before stopping the runtime.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Authentication completion waits for these RPCs. For Connector-enabled GitHub.com this placement is newly reached, but it replaces the prior shared subprocess restart path rather than adding work on top of it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve Copilot SKU for the new token
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per accepted changed token, with existing retry behavior only on a later authenticate call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same SKU lookup followed the restart request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Still awaited by authenticate after credential propagation; unchanged by the PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stop/restart shared Copilot runtime for Enterprise, credential-mode change, cleared credentials, or failed static updates
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one coalesced pending restart across reasons, deferred until all live work is idle. Ordinary same-mode GitHub.com Connector rotation now causes zero restarts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every GitHub.com Connector token change selected client authentication and therefore requested this restart.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No longer blocks subsequent GitHub.com Connector create/restore after successful same-mode rotation; preserved for cases that still require client-owned authentication or recovery.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of currently live resident static-token sessions after deduplication by the live-session map. Unchanged tokens are suppressed by the workbench auth-token cache, and refreshable/provider-backed sessions contribute zero setCredentials calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Credential versions are globally sequenced. Within one version, static-session setCredentials RPCs run sequentially; this existing loop now also applies when Connectors are enabled. Credential-mode changes and Enterprise updates retain deferred global restart semantics.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The per-connection auth-token cache coalesces identical in-flight credentials and suppresses completed unchanged tokens. Static sessions update their captured token after a successful RPC; provider-backed sessions read the shared provider. Failed updates request the existing safe restart fallback.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for cardinality and serialization: the loop, SDK RPC implementation, credential-mode guard, and auth cache are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The resident static-session count and per-RPC duration vary. Although the newly reached loop is sequential, token changes are cache-deduplicated and infrequent, and it replaces a global subprocess teardown plus cross-chat wait; evidence does not establish a net regression warranting a finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The only newly reached fan-out is bounded to resident static-token sessions and substitutes for a demonstrably more disruptive global restart; provider-backed rotations avoid the fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dispose or cancel a remote chat-session restore while it is waiting for an idle/new-task slice
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Remote session resolution and initial history retrieval occur before constructing the restorer. History model mutations then run in bounded local slices; disposal now cancels the restorer-owned token so a pending scheduler wait rejects immediately rather than waiting for the scheduled callback or parent service cancellation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve or create the remote chat session and obtain its history
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider resolution/load for a cold resource; concurrent/repeated loads reuse the resource model/load path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same remote-session load occurred before replay.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Precedes restorer construction and is unaffected by the changed cancellation source.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Schedule idle/new-task callbacks for cooperative history mutation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One scheduled callback per exhausted slice or publication deferral; at most one wait is pending for a restorer at a time.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A disposed restorer's pending wait remained governed only by the broader service token and could survive until its scheduler callback fired.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Callbacks pace model restoration. Disposal now cancels the pending wait immediately, shortening rather than extending lifetime.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One CancellationTokenSource and at most one pending scheduled wait per restorer; replay CPU/model mutations scale with history items as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each restorer advances one generator cooperatively, yielding after a 40 ms budget. Loads are shared per session resource by the chat service. The new cancellation does not add parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Published chat models are reused by session resource; the changed token has no cache interaction. The new source is registered with and disposed by the restorer lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ownership registration and token propagation directly show cancellation on dispose.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: History length and host-idle timing vary, but the changed allocation is constant per restorer and deterministically disposed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The small per-restorer token allocation closes a pending-wait cleanup gap and bounds callback/model retention after disposal.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and all diff pages. Traced Connector create/resume, credential rotation, client restart/subprocess lifecycle, per-session SDK RPC fan-out, reconciliation/catalog refresh, and remote-history restoration cleanup. No actionable performance regression was introduced. Recorded the PR's concrete fix for the prior Connector token-rotation restart regression and its introducing commit.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
